# Completed C3 retained receipt replay

[`completed_c3.run_fixed_c3_receipts`](completed_c3.py) accepts the typed completed-run stage and archive projection, selects the exact C3 application and C3Sdk lifecycle roles from the closed 37-artifact inventory, verifies their staged bytes and ZIP member projections, extracts both into one fresh private area, and cleans only invocation-owned nodes. The internal [`replay_extracted_c3`](completed_c3.py) helper supports a provider harness that has already verified each original archive's name, run, attempt, size, and SHA-256. Both paths require private disjoint extraction roots, identical `source.json` bytes in both artifacts, and the complete clean source checkout to match the capture before loading any new callback.

After source verification, the helper loads the source-owned [`retained_application.validate`](../issue779-checkpoint3/retained_application.py) and [`lifecycle_stalls.validate_retained_receipt`](../issue779-checkpoint3/lifecycle_stalls.py) callbacks, plus the existing output parsers from [`run-native.py`](../issue779-checkpoint3/run-native.py). The native C3 application closeout and the lifecycle-stall closeout call those same callbacks after all existing live process, account, filesystem, and deadline checks have succeeded. The callbacks validate retained receipts, logs, schemas, case ordering, output EOF/accounting, markers, and recorded cleanup facts. They do not acquire a process identity or prove a cgroup, NSS, or filesystem fact from serialized data alone.

The application artifact uses its existing 135-file and 96 MiB retention ceiling. Its two selected Coverlet JSON reports may be up to 32 MiB and its combined Cobertura XML up to 40 MiB; other leaves retain the original 8 MiB cap. The SDK lifecycle artifact keeps its separate 26-file and 32 MiB bound. This replay adds no producer, output, process, or package quota. It does not rerun a native control or extend any original deadline.

The immutable [`C3ReceiptProjection`](completed_c3.py) carries both run-bound artifact identities, source capture, receipt digests, fixed case lists, and literal false native-acceptance and Trusted-eligibility fields. It is mechanism data only. It is not a runtime admission input, accepted proof, measurement result, or coverage gate input.

## Limits and source compatibility

The new callbacks must be present in the exact captured source revision to qualify as a source-bound completed-run replay. The authentic run-109 artifact capture is from revision `64e25cb4`; running the current extracted callback code over those old bytes is only a regression test of the adapter and does not establish that the callbacks were present or invoked in run 109. A new successful source-bound Linux run is required to establish callback execution from the captured source.

This slice replays the seven original C3 application cases, six workspace guards, and three SDK lifecycle rows. It does not validate the separate SDK test-failure diagnostic observation, complete C3 measured-segment chain, C4 account creation or rollback, all other completed-run roles, unchanged solution/Codecov gates, downstream protected qualification, or human acceptance. In particular, a retained manifest that references a coverage report does not prove that report's bytes are present or valid. See the [completed-run inventory](completed-run-README.md), the [completed artifact projection](completed-validation-README.md), and the [57-group plan](../../docs/plans/issue-779-evidencehost-test-plan.md) for remaining independent evidence.
